title: [observability] A check-tests rejection names its failing tests (GitHub #28): the record's reason and note say "check-tests.sh failed: <test>" for each test check-tests.sh failed, from the gate output the record already holds
prompt:
Spawn, mission 4, objective 129 [observability]: a check-tests rejection names its failing tests where the reader sees it (GitHub #28). When the gate rejects a task because check-tests.sh fails, the task's last gate, the note sent back and the integrator's record say "check-tests.sh failed: <test>" for each test that failed, taken from the gate output the record already holds.

Where things stand. A rejection by check-tests.sh reads, on the Missions page's task row ("last gate"), in the task panel, in the timeline and in the note the worker gets back: "regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate". Which test failed is in the gate's output, which the record keeps in full (`log`) and whose tail the note quotes. The reader has to find check-tests.sh's FAILED lines in up to 60 lines of output, or open the gate log. check-tests.sh already prints one line per failing test, `FAILED <test>: <first message line>`, last in its section (rsi/scenarios/check-tests.sh). The integrator already reads them (integrate/host.rs `check_tests_failures`, which the host-fault rule uses), but only to classify the failure, never to say it.

Read: crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/verdicts.rs (`rejected_fields`, `rejection`, `unjudged_head`), integrate/host.rs (`CHECK_TESTS_REGRESSION`, `check_tests_failures`), integrate.rs (where `rejected_fields` is called, and where a host fault is decided before it), and integrate/host_fault_tests.rs.

Required behaviour.
- The record of a rejection whose gate reason is check-tests.sh's regression (it starts with "regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate") names each test check-tests.sh failed, as `check_tests_failures` reads them from the gate's output: its FAILED lines, else the failures its excerpt shows. Each is named in the order the output gives them (check-tests.sh prints one line per failing test).
- The reason reads "check-tests.sh failed: <test>", joined by "; ", for the first five tests. With more, "; and <n> more" follows. Then the gate's own reason follows in brackets:
  "check-tests.sh failed: bb::alpha::adds_up; check-tests.sh failed: bb::beta::keeps_order (regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate)".
- The note quotes that reason, as it quotes every reason: "The gate rejected this work: <reason>.", then the output's tail as today.
- What stays as it is:
  - every other reason;
  - a check-tests.sh rejection whose output names no test;
  - the gate's verdict and its output (gate.sh is not changed; Flake Doctor and every reader of gate logs read the same lines);
  - the host-fault decision, which still compares the gate's own reason;
  - every record field but `reason` and the `note` that quotes it;
  - the store, the API and the web: the reason reaches the task row, the task panel, the timeline and `/api/missions` as every reason does.
- One place makes the reason, in the path every rejection's record takes (`rejected_fields`), so the merge's rejection, a rejection that stands after the work is judged alone, and a stale one name the tests alike.

Unit tests (spawn-cli, in integrate/host_fault_tests.rs beside the output helpers):
- two FAILED lines: the reason and the note's first line exactly as above;
- seven: five named, then "and 2 more";
- no FAILED line, one panicked test in the excerpt (as check-j10-verdicts.sh's 020 prints it): "check-tests.sh failed: t (regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate)";
- another scenario's reason: unchanged;
- check-tests.sh's reason with an output naming no test: unchanged.
Each rule removed alone must fail a test or the scenario.

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/verdicts.rs and crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate/host_fault_tests.rs. One crate. The throwaway is +91 −1 (39 of code and doc comments, 52 of test), within the size guide.

No polled read changes: the reason is written once per gate, and every reader reads the same field as today.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/129.sh. Black box on its own database, with a recording gate (SPAWN_GATE) and made-up work: three gated missions, each on its own source, one reported task each. The gate rejects each candidate as its case.txt says: check-tests.sh with two FAILED lines, check-tests.sh with seven, or 046.sh. One `spawn integrate --once` pass judges them, and `spawn serve` answers the Missions page's reads.
(1) /api/missions: the two-failure task's last gate is rejected, its reason exactly "check-tests.sh failed: bb::alpha::adds_up; check-tests.sh failed: bb::beta::keeps_order (regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate)".
(2) /api/missions/task/<id>: its review_note begins "The gate rejected this work: <that reason>.".
(3) The seven-failure task's reason names bb::t::case_1 to bb::t::case_5, then "; and 2 more (regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate)".
(4) The 046.sh task's reason is exactly "regression: 046.sh fails on the candidate".
(5) The note's tail still quotes the gate's own verdict line, {"verdict":"rejected","reason":"regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate"}.
On main 15ee9707, 129.sh exits 1 with 3 checks failed, the first "(1) task 1's last gate reason: expected [check-tests.sh failed: bb::alpha::adds_up; check-tests.sh failed: bb::beta::keeps_order (regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate)], got [regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate]", then (2) and (3).
check-tests.sh and check-clippy.sh must pass, and so must check-j10-verdicts.sh (whose 020 part rejects by check-tests.sh's output).

Verified by: the gate runs 129.sh on the candidate. After the landing, the lead reads one real `task.gated` rejected record whose gate failed check-tests.sh (the next one the fleet makes, or the latest after the landing). Its reason names the failing tests as check-tests.sh's FAILED lines in its log say, and the task row's "last gate" on the Missions page reads the same. The lead posts it in sync.
